questions.question_text: Which of the following biological treatments was not an empirical discovery?
questions.explanation: Malaria therapy was for general paralysis.

questions.question_text: The term 'demence precoce' was introduced by:
questions.explanation: Be´ne´dict Morel, a French psychiatrist, introduced the term 'de ´mence pre´coce'. Kraepelin later made it into the dementia precox.

questions.question_text: Bleuler's four 'A's exclude:
questions.explanation: Altruism is not one of the four 'A's.

questions.question_text: Schneider's first-rank symptoms do not include:
questions.explanation: Thought block is not a first-rank symptom.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false in the axial system of DSM-IV?

options.text: Axis 3 provides information about mental retardation
Axis 4 is used to describe environmental factors
Axis 2 provides information about personality disorder
Axis 5 is a rating scale called Global Assessment of Function
Axis 1 provides information about major mental disorder

correct_answer.text: Axis 3 provides information about mental retardation

correct_answers.text: Axis 3 provides information about mental retardation

questions.explanation: Axis 2 provides information about personality disorder and mental retardation, while axis 3 provides information about general medical condition.

questions.question_text: The term 'catatonia' was coined by:
questions.explanation: Kahlbaum described catatonia in 1874.

questions.question_text: The term 'hebephrenia' was coined by:
questions.explanation: Hecker described hebephrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following features is not part of the type 1 syndrome described by Crow:

options.text: Presumed dysfunction in the dopamine system

questions.explanation: Structural abnormalities are seen in type 2 syndrome.

questions.question_text: Erikson's stages of psychosocial development do not include:
questions.explanation: Erikson's stage 4 of psychosocial development is industry versus inferiority. Autonomy versus shame and doubt is stage 2.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Freud's psychosexual stages of development is false?

options.text: The oral stage is characterized by dependence
The phallic stage is characterized by obsessionality
The anal stage is characterized by orderliness
The oral stage is characterized by envy
The phallic stage is characterized by competitiveness

correct_answer.text: The phallic stage is characterized by obsessionality

correct_answers.text: The phallic stage is characterized by obsessionality

questions.explanation: Anal stage relates to obsessionality. According to Freud, incomplete resolution of the stages leads to pathological traits in adulthood.

questions.question_text: In which stage of Piaget's model does a child understand that the same volume of water can be contained in a tall jar as in a broad jar?
questions.explanation: Development of logical thought and laws of conservation are attained by the concrete operational stage.

questions.question_text: Gestalt principles do not include:
questions.explanation: Figure–ground differentiation is included in Gestalt's principles. It is ability to differentiate the figure from the background in a picture.

questions.question_text: According to Maslow's hierarchy of needs:

options.text: Aesthetic needs can be achieved after cognitive needs
Physiological or physical needs can be achieved after safety needs
Esteem comes before belonging and love
Self-actualization can be achieved before aesthetic needs
Esteem is achieved after cognitive needs

correct_answer.text: Aesthetic needs can be achieved after cognitive needs

correct_answers.text: Aesthetic needs can be achieved after cognitive needs

questions.explanation: Maslow's hierarchy of needs consists of physiological/physical, safety, social, esteem, cognitive, aesthetic, and self-actualization needs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a part of the social power described by French and Raven?
questions.explanation: Coercion is the fifth type of social power.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false?

options.text: There is more liking within the group in democratic leadership
There is good interaction with the leader in laissez-faire leadership
In democratic leadership, the group can continue in the absence of the leader
Urgent tasks are better done by autocratic leadership
Task completion is poor in laissez-faire leadership

correct_answer.text: There is good interaction with the leader in laissez-faire leadership

correct_answers.text: There is good interaction with the leader in laissez-faire leadership

questions.explanation: Interaction with the leader is poor in laissez-faire leadership.

questions.question_text: According to Sigmund Freud's earliest model:

options.text: Unconscious is governed by the reality principle
Information is readily available from the unconscious
Preconscious content can be brought into consciousness through selective attention

correct_answer.text: Preconscious content can be brought into consciousness through selective attention

correct_answers.text: Preconscious content can be brought into consciousness through selective attention

questions.explanation: Preconscious and conscious involve a secondary process and are governed by the reality principle. Unconscious entails primary process thinking and is governed by the pleasure principle.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false regarding Freud's structural model?

options.text: Id functions at all three levels of conscious, preconscious and unconscious
Superego is the person's values, morals and ethics derived from parents
Id is the unconscious reserve of impulses
Ego is the part that mediates with the external world
Superego develops in the second year of life

correct_answer.text: Id functions at all three levels of conscious, preconscious and unconscious

correct_answers.text: Id functions at all three levels of conscious, preconscious and unconscious

questions.explanation: This theory was initiated by Cade in 1949 but it was too controversial at that time. It later became popular in the 1960s.

questions.question_text: Find the odd one out:
questions.explanation: Anna Freud was involved in describing defense mechanisms. Alfred Adler was the founder of individual psychology.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an autosomal recessive disorder?
questions.explanation: Lesch–Nyhan syndrome is an X-linked recessive disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true?

options.text: No conscious recollection or temporal awareness is needed in implicit retrieval
External locus of control is associated with poor response to stress
Secondary reinforcement is not based on prior learning
Internal locus relates to a feeling that life is externally controlled and determined
People with type A personality are very relaxed

correct_answer.text: External locus of control is associated with poor response to stress

correct_answers.text: External locus of control is associated with poor response to stress

questions.explanation: External locus relates to the feeling that life is externally controlled. Type A personalities are very anxious.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true?

options.text: Disability is the stable persistent limitation of physical or psychological function
Impairment refers to a pathological deficit
Handicap refers to continuing social dysfunction

questions.explanation: All three statements are true.

questions.question_text: Regarding the ICD-10 classification system, which of the following is false?

options.text: It is available in different versions
It is available in all widely spoken languages

questions.explanation: ICD-10 is a categorical classification.

questions.question_text: Regarding DSM-IV, which is true?

options.text: The criteria do not include social consequences of impairment
It is published by the American Psychiatric Association
It is available in widely spoken languages

correct_answer.text: It is published by the American Psychiatric Association

correct_answers.text: It is published by the American Psychiatric Association

questions.explanation: DSM-IV is available only in a single version for both clinical and research purposes. It is available only in English and is a multi-axial system.

questions.question_text: An elderly man in the postoperative ward has been presenting with fluctuating cognition for the last 24 hours. Staff also reported that he has been seen to respond to hallucinations. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Delirium is the most usual presentation in a postoperative ward.

questions.question_text: Regarding Rett syndrome, which of the following is false?

options.text: There is loss of acquired hand skills and speech
It usually involves abnormal early development
There is deceleration in head growth
Onset begins between 7 and 24 months of age
It is reported only in girls

correct_answer.text: It usually involves abnormal early development

correct_answers.text: It usually involves abnormal early development

questions.explanation: Rett syndrome features normal early development.

questions.question_text: Asperger's syndrome is:

options.text: A specific developmental disorder of speech and language
A specific developmental disorder of scholastic skills

questions.explanation: Asperger's syndrome is a pervasive developmental disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding ICD-10 classification?

options.text: Lewy body dementia is not classified in the dementia category
CT scan is diagnostic in Alzheimer's dementia
Dementia beginning before the age of 55 years is classified as dementia in Alzheimer's disease with early onset
Typically symptoms should be present for at least 1 year for confident clinical diagnosis of dementia
Delirium superimposed on dementia is classified under the organic amnestic syndrome not induced by alcohol and other psychoactive substances

correct_answer.text: Lewy body dementia is not classified in the dementia category

correct_answers.text: Lewy body dementia is not classified in the dementia category

questions.explanation: ICD-10 classifies only dementia in Parkinson's disease.

questions.question_text: According to ICD-10, all of the following should be present for a diagnosis of dependence syndrome, except:

options.text: Symptoms should be present at some time during the previous year
The desire to take the particular substance is absent currently

correct_answer.text: The desire to take the particular substance is absent currently

correct_answers.text: The desire to take the particular substance is absent currently

questions.explanation: A strong desire or sense of compulsion to take the substance should be present for a diagnosis of dependence syndrome.

questions.question_text: For a diagnosis of catatonic schizophrenia, predominant behaviours need to include all the following according to ICD-10, except:
questions.explanation: Depression is not a feature of catatonia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false regarding post-schizophrenic depression?

options.text: Depressive symptoms should have been present for at least 2 weeks
It is classified under schizophrenia, schizotypal and delusional disorders
No symptoms of schizophrenia should be present now
The patient should have had schizophrenia in the last year
Depressive symptoms should be prominent and distressing

correct_answer.text: No symptoms of schizophrenia should be present now

correct_answers.text: No symptoms of schizophrenia should be present now

questions.explanation: Some schizophrenic symptoms are still present in post-schizophrenic depression.

questions.question_text: In ICD-10, psychotic disorder as a result of mental and behaviour disorders due to use of alcohol includes all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Alcoholic dementia is not classified in psychotic disorder, but is classified in residual and late-onset psychotic disorder.

questions.question_text: Regarding phobias, which of the following is false?

options.text: Claustrophobia is a fear of closed spaces
Arachnophobia is a fear of spiders
Cynophobia is a fear of dogs
Acrophobia is a fear of open spaces
Hydrophobia is a fear of water

correct_answer.text: Acrophobia is a fear of open spaces

correct_answers.text: Acrophobia is a fear of open spaces

questions.explanation: Acrophobia is fear of heights.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true according to ICD-10 diagnostic criteria?

options.text: In delusional disorder, symptoms must have been present for at least 1 month
In depression, symptoms should have been present for at least 1 week
In hypomania, symptoms should have been present for at least several days
In mania, symptoms should have been present for at least 2 weeks
In acute schizophrenia-like psychotic disorder, symptoms last for more than 1 month

correct_answer.text: In hypomania, symptoms should have been present for at least several days

correct_answers.text: In hypomania, symptoms should have been present for at least several days

questions.explanation: In mania, symptoms should have been present for at least 1 week. In depression, symptoms should have been present for at least 2 weeks. In acute schizophrenia-psychotic disorder, symptoms last for less than 1 month. In delusional disorder, symptoms must have been present for at least 3 months.

questions.question_text: Regarding diagnosis of anorexia nervosa, which of the following is false?

options.text: If onset is prepubertal, pubertal changes are arrested that are irreversible
A widespread endocrine disorder involving the hypothalamo-pituitary-gonadal axis is seen
Body weight is maintained at least 15% below that expected
Weight loss is self-induced by avoidance of 'fattening food'

correct_answer.text: If onset is prepubertal, pubertal changes are arrested that are irreversible

correct_answers.text: If onset is prepubertal, pubertal changes are arrested that are irreversible

questions.explanation: With recovery, puberty is often completed normally.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true?

options.text: Hypochondriacal disorder is the same as somatization disorder
Ganser syndrome is a type of dissociative disorder
Neurasthenia is a type of somatoform disorder
Nightmare is a type of sleep terror
Somatoform disorder is a type of somatization disorder

correct_answer.text: Ganser syndrome is a type of dissociative disorder

correct_answers.text: Ganser syndrome is a type of dissociative disorder

questions.explanation: Somatization disorder is a type of somatoform disorder. In somatization emphasis is on symptoms, while in hypochondriacal disorder emphasis is on the presence of a disease. Neurasthenia comes under 'other neurotic disorder'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following does not come under 'Other anxiety disorder' in ICD-10?
questions.explanation: PTSD comes under 'Reaction to severe stress and adjustment disorders'.

questions.question_text: All of the following are classified into 'Schizophrenia, schizotypal and delusional disorder' in ICD-10, except:
questions.explanation: Schizoid personality disorder comes under 'Specific personality disorder'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false regarding the symptom and the associated personality disorder?

options.text: Callous concern for feeling of others–Dissocial

questions.explanation: Recurrent suspicion is seen commonly in 'Paranoid personality disorder'.

questions.question_text: All of the following are types of 'Other somatoform disorders' in ICD-10, except:
questions.explanation: Psychogenic backache comes under 'Persistent somatoform pain disorder'.

questions.question_text: Schizotypal disorder consists of all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: There is no dominant or typical disturbance in schizotypal disorder.

questions.question_text: All of the following culture-bound syndromes are correctly matched with their corresponding areas, except:
questions.explanation: Brain fag is seen in West African students.

questions.question_text: Regarding ghost sickness, which of the following is false?

options.text: Subjects may say they have been 'bewitched'
Subjects may have a sense of suffocation
It is a preoccupation with death
It is seen in native Africans

correct_answer.text: It is seen in native Africans

correct_answers.text: It is seen in native Africans

questions.explanation: Ghost sickness is seen in Native Americans.

questions.question_text: Amok consists of all of the following, except:

options.text: It may be preceded by a period of depression
The subject is amnesic about the violent acts
The subject always has delusions or another thought disorder
The subject may commit suicide later
It involves sudden, unprovoked, random acts of violence

correct_answer.text: The subject always has delusions or another thought disorder

correct_answers.text: The subject always has delusions or another thought disorder

questions.explanation: Amok is a sudden random attack of violence that may be preceded by a period of depression or anxiety.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true regarding latah, except:

options.text: It occurs predominantly in elderly women
It may be a symptom of disease
It is an exaggerated startle reaction

correct_answer.text: It occurs predominantly in elderly women

correct_answers.text: It occurs predominantly in elderly women

questions.explanation: Latah is predominantly seen in young girls.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true of piblokto?

options.text: It occurs following the actual loss of someone or something
It is also known as Antarctic hysteria
It may be preceded by convulsions or coma
There is never any associated amnesia of the event
It is usually seen in Arctic men

correct_answer.text: It occurs following the actual loss of someone or something

correct_answers.text: It occurs following the actual loss of someone or something

questions.explanation: Piblokto is also known as 'Arctic hysteria' and is seen in polar Eskimo women.

questions.question_text: According to Littlewood and Lipsedge (1987), culture-bound syndromes share all of the following characteristics, except:

options.text: They have a symbolic cultural significance
They usually occur in young men or women
They show a typical triphasic pattern
They are usually dramatic, and the individual is unaware or not responsible
They occur in people who are 'powerful' and socially very accepted

correct_answer.text: They occur in people who are 'powerful' and socially very accepted

correct_answers.text: They occur in people who are 'powerful' and socially very accepted

questions.explanation: Culture-bound syndromes are usually seen in 'powerless' and socially neglected young men or women.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true regarding ashanti, except:

options.text: It is seen usually in women
It may follow a difficult childbirth or death of the child
It is also known as brain fag
A frenzied guilt and fear subtype may follow physical illness and fever

correct_answer.text: It is also known as brain fag

correct_answers.text: It is also known as brain fag

questions.explanation: Brain fag is a syndrome seen in West African students.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding wendigo?

options.text: It is a very common syndrome
It is seen in East Africans
The subject is respected by other people on being transformed
It is a delusion of being transformed into a giant monster

correct_answer.text: It is a delusion of being transformed into a giant monster

correct_answers.text: It is a delusion of being transformed into a giant monster

questions.explanation: Windigo is seen in Native Americans. It is a very uncommon syndrome.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true regarding susto, except:

options.text: It usually follows an acute stressor
It is a belief that the soul has been or will be stolen from the body
It is prevalent in Peru, Mexico and other Latin American countries
It is seen in elderly people
It is characterized by significant body weight loss and sleep disturbance

correct_answer.text: It is seen in elderly people

correct_answers.text: It is seen in elderly people

questions.explanation: Susto is seen in children and adults.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is seen usually in men?
questions.explanation: Amok is seen in Malayan males.
